title: Paracetamol: uses and safety
text: Paracetamol, also called acetaminophen, is used for pain and high temperature. Side effects are uncommon when used correctly. Excess use can seriously harm the liver. Check product ingredients to avoid duplicate paracetamol.

title: Ibuprofen: uses and side effects
text: Ibuprofen reduces pain, inflammation and fever. It can cause stomach upset, nausea, dizziness or rash. Its suitability depends on health conditions and other medicines. Ask a pharmacist before combining medicines.

title: NSAID interaction cautions
text: NSAIDs such as ibuprofen can interact with anticoagulants and medicines used to lower blood pressure. A pharmacist needs the exact medicine names to review a combination. An incomplete database cannot establish safety.

title: Warfarin information
text: Warfarin is an anticoagulant used to prevent and treat blood clots. Bleeding is an important risk. Other medicines can affect treatment. Ask the prescribing clinician or pharmacist before changing medicines.

title: WHO: medication safety
text: Medication safety is a patient-safety priority. WHO’s Medication Without Harm initiative addresses avoidable harm from unsafe medication practices and errors.

title: Emergency warning signs
text: Chest pain spreading to an arm or jaw, severe breathing difficulty and unresponsiveness require emergency assessment. Contact local emergency services immediately; do not wait for an online answer or drive yourself.

title: Generic ingredient example
text: The cited US Tylenol Regular Strength tablet label lists acetaminophen as its active ingredient. Acetaminophen is also called paracetamol. Brand variants may contain different ingredients. A pharmacist must check the exact product, strength and formulation before any substitution; this project does not compare prices.
